title: The Gigantic Turnip
note: A new adaptation of the cumulative Russian turnip tale, retaining its chain of helpers and repeated pulling pattern.

rights.basis: Source edition published in 1915 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A family and their animals pull together on the leaves of an enormous turnip.
scenes: Grandfather planted a turnip seed. Rain fell, sun shone, and the turnip grew broad leaves, a round purple crown, and a root as big as a barrel.
Grandfather pulled. The turnip stayed. Grandmother held Grandfather, and they pulled together. Still it would not move.
Their granddaughter joined, then the dog, then the cat. They leaned back in one long line. The turnip only wiggled.
At last a tiny mouse took hold of the cat’s tail. “Ready?” called Grandfather. Everyone pulled: mouse, cat, dog, granddaughter, grandmother, grandfather.
Out popped the turnip, and down tumbled the whole line—laughing.
There was turnip soup enough for everyone, including one very small but very important mouse.
